Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-16
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Serena Kaur (Aventra Head of Data Privacy), Ethan Morales (Aventra Infra), Jules Fontaine (Aventra Legal)

Summary (auto):
- Deep dive on data handling, retention windows for prompts and transcripts, KMS and encryption at rest, RBAC/SSO, audit log granularity, and explicit confirmation on model training policies.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to deliver SOC2/ISO docs and BAA; Aventra to provide sample prompts; schedule VPC demo.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and then we'll jump in.
[00:10] Dr. Serena: Hi, Serena here. I'm Head of Data Privacy at Aventra.
[00:14] Ethan: Ethan, infra.
[00:16] Jules: Jules, legal.
[00:18] Liam (SE): Liam from Redwood, good to meet you all.
[00:22] Maya: Ok great. Today's goal — confirm security posture, especially how customer data is handled around prompt retention and model training, plus KMS/SSO and audit logs.
[00:33] Dr. Serena: Right. Our main question is, do you ever use our prompts or outputs to fine tune or train models in your hosted service? We need an explicit non-consumption assurance for our compliance reviewers.
[00:45] Maya: Short answer — we do not use customer prompts or responses to train our shared models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a contractual training program. By default the hosted inference plane is non-training, we keep data isolated and it's not added to training corpora.
[00:58] Jules: Can you point to the clause or doc? Our legal needs something contractual.
[01:04] Maya: Yes, we'll send the BAA and the security FAQ excerpt. We'll include the exact language — "Redwood will not use customer data to train models unless customer provides explicit written opt-in."
[01:12] Ethan: When you say "not used", is that both for transient prompts and for logs — like are request logs retained for troubleshooting?
[01:21] Liam: We keep short-lived metadata and traces for debugging and SLOs. By default payloads (full prompt/content) are ephemeral and purged according to the customer retention policy. For hosted customers we retain transcripts only for X days by default — configurable — and you can opt for zero retention where we only persist encrypted audit events.
[01:38] Dr. Serena: What's X here? We need max retention values for PHI workloads.
[01:43] Liam: Default is 30 days for hosted dev accounts; enterprise agreements can set 0, 7, or 30 days. For private/VPC installs you control retention fully. We'll put these exact numbers in the follow-up doc.
[01:54] Jules: And encryption — who holds the keys? We require customer-managed keys for production PHI.
[01:59] Maya: We support Redwood-managed keys by default, and customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private options. For VPC/private on-prem we support bringing your own key material with HSM integration.
[02:10] Ethan: Is that integrated with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault?
[02:13] Liam: Yes — we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Google Cloud KMS. For BYOK with HSM we have a guided onboarding flow and can provide runbooks.
[02:23] Dr. Serena: Audit logging is crucial. We need immutable logs for all admin actions and key rotations. Can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[02:31] Liam: Absolutely. We stream audit events to customer endpoints (S3, SIEM via syslog/HTTPS) and retain a copy for 90 days by default in hosted. Enterprise can extend that. Logs include who/what/when for role actions, model deployments, key rotation, and RBAC changes. PVC — sorry, VPC specific — for private installs you can elect to disable retention in Redwood control plane and only keep logs locally.
[02:52] Ethan: You said "who/what/when" — do logs contain prompt content?
[02:56] Maya: No, content is excluded from audit events unless the customer configures full payload retention. Typically audit events contain request IDs, user ids, model id, timestamps, error/tracing info, and token counts. We can redact or hash prompt content in the logs.
[03:10] Dr. Serena: Hashing may still be a concern if PHI is in the prompt. What redaction options do you offer?
[03:15] Liam: We offer pre-send redaction hooks, regex-based PII scrubbing, and a client-side SDK helper that can pseudonymize before it leaves the customer environment. For highest assurance we recommend pseudonymization client-side + BYOK and zero retention on the server.
[03:30] Jules: For legal sign-off, we also need confirmation on SOC 2 and ISO. Are you SOC 2 Type II and do you have ISO 27001?
[03:38] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and are ISO 27001 audited. We'll attach the latest reports. We'll also attach a short controls mapping to common artifacts you may request.
[03:47] Ethan: Is there an Audit trail for access to keys and who uses them?
[03:51] Liam: KMS operations are logged; key usage events and access are auditable via both Redwood control plane and your cloud KMS logs. On dedicated/private we're flexible — you can retain a master log in your SIEM.
[04:02] Dr. Serena: Network isolation — for private deployment, does your control plane see any plaintext prompts?
[04:07] Maya: For Private with full air-gap, the control plane is customer-hosted — Redwood provides the orchestration bundle but the data path stays inside your network. For VPC-hosted we still offer a private control-plane option that only exchanges health and metric telemetry; payloads are always direct between customer and inference nodes under your VPC.
[04:26] Ethan: Ok. Now a bit about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta, need SCIM and SAML SSO plus fine-grained RBAC per environment.
[04:34] Liam: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning, and RBAC maps to roles (admin, deployer, observer, auditor). We can create custom roles and map attributes from Okta groups. All actions tied to user identity.
[04:46] Jules: For legal we need demonstration that access delegation won't allow cross-tenant data leakage between Aventra projects.
[04:52] Liam: Tenancy is isolated at the application and data layer for dedicated and private installs. In hosted we have strong multi-tenant isolation and per-tenant namespaces; we will provide the separation architecture diagram.
[05:03] Dr. Serena: A few practical scenarios — our support team may need to replay a session to troubleshoot. How do you handle support access?
[05:10] Maya: Redwood support access is gated via Just-In-Time access and audited. For hosted enterprise customers we use ticketed, time-bound access with customer approval and MFA. For private installs, we provide runbooks for on-prem assistance without direct access.
[05:24] Ethan: What about derivative content? If a user asks the model to summarize a patient record, does the system treat the summary differently than the original PHI?
[05:33] Liam: From a data handling standpoint both prompt and response are considered customer data. Summaries are retained per the same retention policy. For classification/regression outputs that you want to keep, we recommend storing them in your own datastore; Redwood isn't changing classification that would strip PHI unless you configure redaction.
[05:50] Dr. Serena: Do you support a "no indexing" flag — something that ensures we never ingest for training even if logs are enabled?
[05:58] Maya: Yes — we have a "do-not-index" and "zero-retention" flags at the request/route level. We'll document the API header for that and sample SDK usage. It's included in enterprise controls and private deployments.
[06:10] Jules: For contract language, we need a warranty clause that confirms no training without written opt-in plus breach notification timeline.
[06:17] Maya: We'll loop in legal and include suggested language; standard breach notification is 72 hours after detection — we can mirror your SLAs as negotiated.
[06:26] Ethan: Are there any edge cases where telemetry could be used for model improvement? For example, aggregated performance stats?
[06:33] Liam: Aggregated, anonymized telemetry (e.g., latency distributions, token length histograms) may be used to improve system performance. That telemetry does not contain PII or prompt content. We'll include details on anonymization thresholds.
[06:46] Dr. Serena: Ok. A quick check on data residency — our data must remain in EU regions for EU customers. Can you pin inference nodes to eu-west-1?
[06:55] Liam: Yes — region pinning is supported. We can ensure inference and logging endpoints are in eu-west-1 or another EU region for tenancy. For private deployments you choose the region/cluster location.
[07:06] Maya: We're almost out of time. Quick recap of the commitments and deliverables?
[07:10] Jules: Please include: SOC2, ISO attestation, BAA, retention config table, API header for do-not-index, RBAC role mapping, and the separation architecture diagram.
[07:20] Maya: We'll send those by Friday (2028-03-18). Liam will schedule the VPC demo, and Ethan will send the sample prompt set.
[07:28] Dr. Serena: Sounds good. One last thing — for our compliance team, could you provide an example redaction regex or SDK snippet?
[07:34] Liam: Yes, we'll include examples: SSN, MRN patterns, and a Node/Python SDK snippet for client-side pseudonymization.
[07:44] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the docs and calendar invites.
[07:48] Jules: Thanks.

End of meeting.
